It's official: Vinnie Keane retires. Undrafted to undeniable, and staying in Grand Lake.

Vinnie Keane made it official this cycle: he is retiring from baseball. The announcement closes a career that went from undrafted to undeniable, with 7 World Series titles in Oakland, an MVP, 7 All-Star selections, 3 Gold Gloves, 5 Silver Sluggers and 436 career homeruns. Keane said goodbye in pieces all season.
Current cycle: C115

He hit a 3-run homer in his final visit to New York, went 4-5 with a 3-run homer in his last regular season at bat to close the record 127-35 season, went 3-4 in a playoff game in Minnesota, and started at third base in the World Series clincher in Philadelphia, driving in a run. The parade in C111 and the Blue Lattern Bar night in C112 felt like the end, but this is the formal announcement. Keane is not leaving Oakland.

He and his wife Amara live in Grand Lake, where the family opened Keane Mercantile, and the Keane Foundation runs the Firehouse 29 West Oakland Baseball Academy and the annual Keane for Kids Gala. His contract ran through 2041, so nothing is left on the books, only a DH/third base spot and a clubhouse voice to replace as Taveras and Quintero take over.
Vinnie Keane — Former Designated Hitter, Oakland A's Legend
